segments.text: Gumgumi sits down on a park bench.
A thermometer shows the armrest and backrest match.
But touching the metal feels much colder.
Skin senses how fast heat leaves it, not temperature.
Metal conducts heat fast, pulling it out of your skin.
Wood conducts heat slowly, so it barely takes any.
That's why skin touching metal cools down fast.
This difference is called thermal conductivity.
Back on the bench, only the metal side feels cold.
Same temperature, but faster heat loss feels colder.
